+name: Autofix PR Comment Handler
+
+on:
+  workflow_run:
+    workflows: ["autofix.ci"]
+    types: [completed]
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+  pull-requests: write
+
+jobs:
+  comment-on-regress-failure:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    if: github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'failure'
+    steps:
+      - name: Download regress check result
+        uses: actions/download-artifact@fa0a91b85d4f404e444e00e005971372dc801d16 # v4
+        with:
+          name: autofix-regress-check
+          github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+          run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
+
+      - name: Check if regress.yml was the issue
+        id: check
+        run: |
+          regress_changed=$(cat regress_changed.txt)
+          pr_number=$(cat pr_number.txt)
+          echo "regress_changed=$regress_changed" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
+          echo "pr_number=$pr_number" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
+
+      - name: Post PR comment about regress.yml
+        if: steps.check.outputs.regress_changed == 'true'
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+        run: |
+          gh pr comment ${{ steps.check.outputs.pr_number }} \
+            --repo ${{ github.repository }} \
+            --body "## ⚠️ Autofix Failed: Workflow File Update Required
+
+          The \`autofix.ci\` check failed because it cannot commit changes to \`.github/workflows/regress.yml\` due to security restrictions.
+
+          **To fix this:**
+
+          1. Run the following command locally:
+             \`\`\`bash
+             ./bin/chore gen regress
+             \`\`\`
+
+          2. Review the changes to \`.github/workflows/regress.yml\`
+
+          3. Commit the changes:
+             \`\`\`bash
+             git add .github/workflows/regress.yml
+             git commit -m \"Regenerate regress workflow\"
+             git push
+             \`\`\`
+
+          The autofix check should pass once the workflow file is updated.
+
+          ---
+          <sub>This is an automated message. The workflow file needs to be regenerated because you modified one of: \`tools/test/regress-tests.yaml\`, \`tools/test/regress-gh-template.yaml\`, or \`tools/test/gen_regress.rb\`.</sub>"
body:
The `gh pr comment --body "..."` value is a multi-line double-quoted string that includes the YAML/script indentation after each newline. Those leading spaces will be preserved in the posted comment and can cause Markdown to render most of the message as an indented code block. Consider switching to `--body-file` (write a temp markdown file via a heredoc) or otherwise constructing the body without leading indentation so the comment renders correctly.
```suggestion
          cat << 'EOF' > pr-comment.md
          ## ⚠️ Autofix Failed: Workflow File Update Required
          
          The `autofix.ci` check failed because it cannot commit changes to `.github/workflows/regress.yml` due to security restrictions.
          
          **To fix this:**
          
          1. Run the following command locally:
             ```bash
             ./bin/chore gen regress
             ```
          
          2. Review the changes to `.github/workflows/regress.yml`
          
          3. Commit the changes:
             ```bash
             git add .github/workflows/regress.yml
             git commit -m "Regenerate regress workflow"
             git push
             ```
          
          The autofix check should pass once the workflow file is updated.
          
          ---
          <sub>This is an automated message. The workflow file needs to be regenerated because you modified one of: `tools/test/regress-tests.yaml`, `tools/test/regress-gh-template.yaml`, or `tools/test/gen_regress.rb`.</sub>
          EOF
          
          gh pr comment ${{ steps.check.outputs.pr_number }} \
            --repo ${{ github.repository }} \
            --body-file pr-comment.md
```

+

body: Security: this workflow_run job trusts an artifact produced by the preceding `pull_request` workflow run to decide both whether to comment and which PR to comment on. Because `pull_request` workflows run with code/workflows from the PR head (including forks), an attacker could modify the autofix workflow in their PR to upload a forged `autofix-regress-check` artifact (e.g., set a different PR number), and this privileged workflow (with `pull-requests: write`) would act on it. Prefer deriving `pr_number` from `github.event.workflow_run.pull_requests[0].number` (or the workflow_run payload) and avoid using artifacts as a trust boundary; if you must keep the artifact, add strict validation (e.g., only run when `github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name == github.repository`) and validate the artifact contents before using them.

+          else

+          fi

       - uses: autofix-ci/action@7a166d7532b277f34e16238930461bf77f9d7ed8 # v1.3.3
+
+      # Save result as artifact for workflow_run to consume
+      - name: Save regress check result
+        if: always()
+        run: |
+          echo "${{ steps.check-regress.outputs.regress_changed }}" > /tmp/regress_changed.txt
+          echo "${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}" > /tmp/pr_number.txt
+
+      - name: Upload regress check result
+        if: always()
+        uses: actions/upload-artifact@b7c566a772e6b6bfb58ed0dc250532a479d7789f # v6
+        with:
+          name: autofix-regress-check
+          path: |

body: Security: uploading `/tmp/pr_number.txt` (and relying on it later in a `workflow_run` workflow with `pull-requests: write`) creates a privilege boundary between an untrusted `pull_request` run and a privileged follow-up workflow. Since `workflow_run` already includes the associated PR(s) in its event payload, avoid persisting the PR number via artifact and instead have the `workflow_run` job read it directly from `github.event.workflow_run.pull_requests`. This reduces the chance of artifact spoofing / cross-workflow injection.

+          std_path_override: udb_gem_root / "test" / "mock_spec" / "isa",

+    # @return [Udb::ConfiguredArchitecture]

+      end
+    end
+
+    # Get a ConfiguredArchitecture from the mock database
+    #
+    # @param config [String] Config name (default "_")
+    # @return [Udb::ConfiguredArchitecture]

+      @mock_cfg_archs ||= {}

+        mock_resolver.cfg_arch_for(config)
+      end
+    end

+    # Some tests may skip if the full database isn't available
+    def real_db_available?

In `real_db_available?`, the `rescue => e` assigns an exception to `e` but never uses it. This can trigger RuboCop’s useless assignment/unused variable cops and adds noise. Consider changing it to `rescue` (or `rescue StandardError`) without binding the exception unless you plan to log it under `UDB_TEST_FIXTURE_DEBUG`.
```suggestion

```
